previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with relapsed multiple myeloma, autoimmune hemolytic anemia, type 2 diabetes, and diastolic heart failure, was admitted for fever and weakness. Evaluation revealed pneumonia and bilateral lower extremity cellulitis. He was treated with IV antibiotics, later transitioned to oral levofloxacin, and received IVIG for low antibody levels. His diabetes required insulin regimen adjustment due to fluctuations. Hypertension was managed with addition of losartan. Renal function remained stable despite baseline CKD, and proteinuria was monitored without biopsy due to bleeding risk. Anemia improved with supportive care. He recovered well, with resolution of fever and respiratory symptoms, and was discharged home on oral antibiotics and optimized medical management with follow-up arranged.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Mr. ___,

You were admitted to the hospital because you passed out at 
home. We believe this was caused vasovagal syncope or fainting. 
You did not have any findings which indicated that your heart or 
an infection were responsible for this episode. You were watched 
in the hospital and had no further episodes of these fainting 
spells.

While you were in the hospital, you also were found to have low 
blood counts that we believe were due to your red blood cells 
bursting. It is not clear what caused this event to happen. Your 
steroids were adjusted slightly, and your blood counts 
stabilized prior to your discharge.

When you are discharged from the hospital, it is important for 
you to take your medication as directed. You had your morning 
dose of insulin glargine (lantus) decreased to 30 units each 
morning. You also started a medication called Vitamin B12 
(Cyanocobalamin) for your anemia. You will follow up with Dr. 
___ this week to continue your treatment for multiple 
myeloma.

All our best,
Your ___ Care Team
